newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland hails progress in EU crime-busting.
newsitem.headline: Ireland hails progress in EU crime-busting.

text.p: Ireland said on Friday there had been substantial progress in agreeing measures to crack down on the scourge of organised crime and drug trafficking, a top priority during its six-month stint as European Union president.

In draft conclusions on the final day of the EU summit in Dublin, the Irish urged member states to keep up the momentum in a bid to develop the 15-country bloc as "an area of freedom, security and justice".
Leaders agreed late on Friday a joint action to boost cooperation between police, customs and judicial authorities in fighting drug addiction and illegal drug trafficking.

A key element to reaching an accord was a deal between France and The Netherlands to put aside their public differences over Dutch tolerance of soft drugs use and work together to combat drug "tourism" and production.
Drugs are illegal in The Netherlands but, under a progressive 20-year experiment, some 1,200 "coffee-shops" are allowed to sell modest amounts of cannabis for personal use.
France argues that this soft approach attracts thousands of youngsters who cross the Dutch border to buy cheap and readily available narcotics which are then circulated in France and elsewhere.

French President Jacques Chirac, a vociferous crusader against the Dutch policy, and his Hague counterpart Wim Kok met privately on Friday to defuse a public row and agreed to work together in the common fight against drugs and crime.

The key elements of the package include better cooperation between police and customs to prevent drug trafficking; tougher sentences for traffickers and cooperation between forensic laboratories in defining drug seizures.
The EU will also take its message to outside parties in an attempt to stem the flood of illicit drugs pouring into the bloc from eastern Europe, the Caribbean, central Asia and Latin America.
"The (summit) confirms the priority it attaches to sustained and coordinated action in the fight against drugs..," the draft said.
The paper also stressed the bloc's determination to fight organised crime and its "abhorrence" at the "odious" sexual exploitation of children and trafficking in humans.
A new high level group will draw up an action plan by next spring to make specific recommendations on how to step up the fight against crime.
The Netherlands, which takes over the EU presidency next month, has also pledged to launch a campaign against racism and xenophobia.
